question: Restate the complete pamphlet-binding plan you proposed for my bench, keeping all numbered stages in order, and include the adhesive and hinge-gap requirements.
body:
For your own pamphlet-binding bench, I propose this complete ordered plan. These steps belong to your bench, not Nadi's. Use reversible wheat paste throughout; do not substitute permanent contact adhesive. Keep the kettle holes at the top and bottom distinct from the three inner sewing holes.
1. Prepare the work surface: Cover the bench with a washable mat and keep drinks on the separate side table.
2. Check the press: Inspect the press boards for raised staples and wipe both faces before any paper touches them.
3. Measure the paper: Use a single card template so each sheet has the same height and grain direction.
4. Cut the sheets: Cut on the waste side of the mark and keep the blade away from the square edge.
5. Fold the sheets: Fold with the grain and crease once with the bone folder instead of rubbing repeatedly.
6. Group the signatures: Nest four folded sheets per signature and mark the outside fold lightly in pencil.
7. Number the signatures: Number them in reading order on the fold, keeping the mark inside the future spine.
8. Make the punching jig: Fold a spare sheet around all five hole positions and label its top edge clearly.
9. Punch the sewing holes: Support each opened signature in a cradle and punch outward through the existing jig marks.
10. Cut the linen thread: Cut one continuous piece long enough for all signatures, with extra length for the final knot.
11. Prepare the sewing supports: Lay two cotton tapes across the press and keep their edges parallel to each other.
12. Start the first signature: Enter from the outside at the bottom kettle hole and leave a short tail for tying.
13. Sew the inner runs: Pass the thread along the inside fold and loop it around each cotton tape without piercing it.
14. Add the next signature: Join each new signature to the preceding one while keeping its pencilled top edge aligned.
15. Sew all the signatures: Continue until every numbered signature is joined, checking the page order before the last knot.
16. Tie the final knot: Tie the final kettle stitch to the preceding signature and trim the loose tail to ten millimetres.
17. Attach the endpapers: Paste only the narrow hinge strip of each endpaper to the first and last signatures.
18. Square the text block: Tap the head and fore edge gently against a flat board until the folded sections are even.
19. Press the text block: Hold the squared block between clean boards for twenty minutes with the spine projecting slightly.
20. Glue the spine: Brush a thin coat of reversible wheat paste along the exposed spine and avoid flooding the folds.
21. Add the gauze support: Lay cotton gauze on the wet spine and leave thirty millimetres of gauze extending on each side.
22. Add the kraft lining: Paste a narrow kraft-paper strip over the gauze and smooth it with the clean brush handle.
23. Dry the block: Leave the block supported upright overnight, keeping the projecting gauze away from the wet spine.
24. Measure the cover boards: Make each board three millimetres taller than the text block and two millimetres wider.
25. Cut the cover boards: Cut both boards from the same sheet and mark their inside faces before stacking them.
26. Cut the spine strip: Make a card strip as wide as the dried spine and as tall as the two cover boards.
27. Lay out the cloth: Place the boards and spine strip on the cloth with a six-millimetre hinge gap on each side.
28. Paste the cloth: Apply paste evenly to the cloth and lift it from the waste sheet before placing the boards.
29. Attach the boards: Place the labelled inside faces upward and check the hinge gaps using the same spacer.
30. Turn in the edges: Turn in the head and tail first, then fold the corners and turn in the fore edges.
31. Dry the cover case: Dry the case under light weight between release sheets until the cloth stops feeling cool.
32. Fit the text block: Test the dry block in the case and check that both boards extend equally above the pages.
33. Attach the gauze wings: Paste the projecting gauze to the inside boards while keeping paste away from both hinge gaps.
34. Paste down the endpapers: Brush paste onto each outer endpaper and close the boards without pulling the paper tight.
35. Protect the wet pages: Insert fresh release sheets beside the pasted endpapers and remove any squeezed-out paste.
36. Set the hinges: Close the book between clean boards with narrow rods resting exactly over the two hinge gaps.
37. Press the completed book: Leave the covered book under gentle weight overnight and change the release sheets once.
38. Check the finished binding: Open only halfway at first and inspect both endpaper hinges for lifting or fresh wrinkles.
